population.note: FICTIONAL. Base of ~270M adults. Current users: 25.2% ≈ 68.0M. Ever-used: 34.0% ≈ 91.8M. Used and now off: 34.0 − 25.2 = 8.8% ≈ 23.8M. New ever-users since 2030: 34.0 − 26.5 = 7.5 pts, of whom 5.6 are on and 1.9 already off. The 2030 cohort of 26.5 pts now has 19.6 on and 6.9 off. Of the 18.8 pts on in 2030, 11.0 stayed on (58.5%, up from ~50% last step because established users persist longer). The other 7.8 stopped, joining the 7.7 already off for a pool of 15.5. Of that pool, 8.6 restarted (55%, the parent's two-year restart rate). 11.0 + 8.6 = 19.6 on; 15.5 − 8.6 = 6.9 off. Totals: on 19.6 + 5.6 = 25.2; off 6.9 + 1.9 = 8.8. Cycled: the 8.9 pts who had cycled by 2030 plus ~3.4 pts of first-time restarts gives 12.3 of 34.0 ever-users = 36%. Many of those first-time stops were structural: the 2×90-day cessation cap, employer plan exclusions at open enrollment, and Medicaid waiver lockouts. Age bands weighted by adult shares (20/33/24/23%): 3.6 + 8.8 + 9.1 + 3.7 = 25.2. The 18–29 band nearly doubled (10→18) on the vaping-cessation label and 'craving-free' subscriptions. Income thirds average (31 + 24.6 + 20)/3 = 25.2. Bottom-third gains came through HRSA, Medicaid, the cessation mandate (smoking and vaping prevalence is highest in this third) and gray product. Middle-third growth was held back most by employer retreat; many in that third moved to TrumpRx cash or onto cessation-coded courses. Off-drug population: ~23.8M ex-users, a growing share of whom stopped because coverage ended rather than by choice, and ~178M never-users. Among never-users, the 'Full Table' and fat-acceptance revival has made opting out a declared identity for an unmeasured but visible minority. Pediatric: 1.3% of ~73M ≈ 950k. About 150k are aged 6–11 (liraglutide-labelled), and roughly 60k are 16–17-year-olds given semaglutide off-label for vaping cessation under adolescent-medicine protocols.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed in Dec 2031 through 2033. Under the Mar 2031 price agreement the payment falls from $275 to $215/month; the copay stays $50, and the DEXA/strength counselling visit for 65+ is retained. Obesity-indication Bridge users number ~3.4M: 3.4M × $215 × 12 ≈ $8.8B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15% of fills ≈ 10.2M users (≈9.9M adults 65+ plus ~0.3M disabled under-65), most of them on diabetes, cardiac, CKD or OSA codes. Medicaid pays ≈11% ≈ 7.5M users at ~$215 net: 7.5M × $215 × 12 ≈ $19.4B/yr combined federal and state. Adherence waivers now run in five states: Indiana and Arkansas unchanged, plus Missouri, Oklahoma and Tennessee approved Jul 2031. The HRSA Community Incretin Access Program was renewed for FY2032 at $5.6B. It serves ≈4.5M users: 2.6M on liraglutide × $70 contract × 12 ≈ $2.2B, plus 1.9M on semaglutide for cessation or AUD × $149 × 12 ≈ $3.4B, ≈ $5.6B total. New conditions require ≥80% PDC refill verification for all users and twice-yearly verified weigh-ins for liraglutide obesity patients.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 80+ semaglutide brands at $6–40/month, and generic tirzepatide has launched in India and Brazil. Generic semaglutide is sold in Canada, Mexico, Turkey, China and much of the EU after 2031 expiries. US entry is set by patent settlements and pediatric exclusivity to 2033.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~68.0M users: commercial 27.9% (19.0M), Medicare 15.0% (10.2M), Medicaid 11.0% (7.5M), HRSA 6.6% (4.5M), cash/direct 20.6% (14.0M), gray 18.8% (12.8M); 19.0 + 10.2 + 7.5 + 4.5 + 14.0 + 12.8 = 68.0M. Commercial users rose in absolute terms while employer weight-management coverage fell from 57% to 44%. Inside commercial, ~9.0M are on diabetes, cardiac, OSA or CKD codes, ~6.0M on mandated cessation or AUD parity courses, and only ~4.0M on weight-management benefits. Price path is managed decline. The Mar 2031 TrumpRx/CMS agreement set cash prices of $249 (semaglutide pen), $299 (tirzepatide) and $149 (oral starter doses of the Wegovy pill and Foundayo). Manufacturers got tariff relief for committed US fill-finish capacity in return. List prices did not move: Wegovy is $1,349 and retatrutide $1,499, still allocated with no portal price. The cash channel grew from 7.0M to 14.0M, mostly middle-third workers dropped by employer plans, plus ~3.0M 'focus/calm' subscribers. Gray share held near 19% because the $249 portal price narrowed but did not close the gap with $129 compounders and $6–40 Indian pens. Rationing works through coverage, not price: the cessation cap of two 90-day courses, Medicaid lockouts and the new HRSA adherence rules.

GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. US generics)

e-cigarette/vaping nicotine dependence in adults (semaglutide injection and Wegovy pill, Feb 2031)

semaglutide for vaping cessation in 16–17-year-olds under adolescent-medicine protocols

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class reached market (driver: none). Survodutide's resubmission drew an advisory committee in Apr 2032 that split on hepatic signals; PDUFA is extended to Q1 2033. Amycretin was resubmitted in Mar 2031 after Novo's North Carolina site cleared reinspection; an FDA information request on long-term pancreatic endpoints, issued after the 2032 EPI signal, pushed the decision into 2033. MariTide (BLA Jul 2030) received a CRL in Jun 2031 over autoinjector human-factors data and dose-escalation tolerability; it was resubmitted in Feb 2032 with a decision expected 2033. Bimagrumab combinations remain in phase 3. The nicotine driver is realised as supplements to existing drugs: semaglutide's cessation label was extended to e-cigarette dependence (sNDA Jun 2030, approved Feb 2031), and orforglipron gained a smoking/vaping cessation indication (sNDA Jun 2031, approved Jun 2032), which puts a $149 small-molecule pill under the ACA preventive mandate.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are higher in gray-market and young vaping-cessation users who escalate fast.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed emptying on drug is established; persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 passed ~61,000 filed and tolled claims. The second bellwether (Oct 2031) went for the defence, and there is no global settlement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. FDA still declines a persistent-gastroparesis label. Reserves were raised again in 2031 annual reports.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid loss; absolute counts keep rising with volume.
Acute pancreatitis is still without causal confirmation and remains a low absolute risk. Plaintiffs now cite the 2032 EPI signal to argue chronic pancreatic injury.
A population problem in 65+, concentrated in unmonitored, low-protein users on HRSA liraglutide and gray product.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label (2028) stands. The Bridge counselling visit is retained. The HRSA renewal added weigh-ins but no body-composition check.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: HR ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term and cycling users, concentrated in women. Interim 6–11 registry data (2032) show bone accrual below age-predicted values, which cannot be interpreted without a control arm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended in 65+ and postmenopausal women. FDA asked for a matched comparator in the pediatric study.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reduced-pleasure reports remain ~10–15% of long-term users, dose-dependent. Lilly's 2031 retatrutide postmarketing readout showed a small dose-dependent SHAPS anhedonia-scale shift at top doses (mean ~1 point; ~6% crossing threshold vs ~3% on comparator). FDA called this hypothesis-generating.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change; FDA requested a dedicated study. The FTC brought two consent orders (2031) against 'calm' brands over unsubstantiated claims, but the products remain legal off-label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven increasingly by coverage events: employer exclusions, cessation caps and five-state Medicaid lockouts.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fat-soluble vitamin (D, A, E) deficiencies now partly overlap with the EPI signal in long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; the Endocrine Society advises annual vitamin D and B12 testing after 3 years.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of follow-up in adults and nine in adolescents. Users with ≥5 years of continuous exposure now number in the millions, which made the EPI signal detectable.
Poison-centre calls plateaued at 2030 levels. Teen vaping-cessation users buying gray pens are a new subgroup.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters and import alerts; first DOJ indictment of a research-peptide distributor (2031); no action against individuals.

safety_ledger.effect: Late-onset exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (EPI) after ≥5 years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: NEW. A Danish–Swedish registry analysis (May 2032) of users with ≥5 years of uninterrupted GLP-1 exposure found incident EPI (low faecal elastase with steatorrhoea or fat-soluble vitamin deficiency) at ~3.1 per 1,000 person-years, against ~1.7 in matched non-users: HR ~1.8, absent before year 4. Diabetes itself raises EPI risk, so confounding is the main counter-argument, but the signal held in non-diabetic obesity users. US claims data show a similar direction. Absolute risk is low; most cases respond to enzyme replacement.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Aug 2032) recommends evaluating long-term users with steatorrhoea or vitamin deficiency. The class label review is open, and EMA PRAC has started a referral. No change to continuous-use guidance; obesity societies note the trade-off with cycling-related bone loss.

food_and_beverage.state: With a quarter of adults on drug, US snack, confectionery and sugary-drink volume keeps falling at roughly the 2028–30 rate. Saturation in the top third slows the decline there while bottom-third uptake extends it. The majors run US volume as a managed decline, sell or spin off sweet-snack units and push protein, fibre and 'small-format' lines. Church and community potluck culture is a small countervailing pocket that the trade press notices.

alcohol.state: AUD parity plus the vaping label hit two sin categories together. Spirits and beer volumes fall again, and non-alcoholic and premium single-serve formats grow. US cigarette volumes fall faster than the long-run trend, and vape-pod makers in the 18–29 market report double-digit declines. Several states revised tobacco-excise forecasts down and moved to backfill Master Settlement-linked budget lines.

restaurants.state: Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual have adapted. Mid-income value chains keep pruning units. Portion-flexible 'half-plate' menus are now standard at casual-dining chains. Bar revenue per cover is down again.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. Athletic-cut tailoring keeps growing, plus-size continues to shrink, and resale platforms absorb the churn of bodies moving both ways as coverage stops and starts.

fitness.state: Strength-and-DEXA studios saturate first-tier metros and add 'pancreatic and vitamin panels' after the EPI communication. Budget gyms gain HRSA and cash users. The gray market in research peptides on gym floors persists.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage falls from 57% to 44% as plans retreat to diabetes, cardiac and OSA codes and the mandated cessation/AUD benefits. Pharmacy trend slows to ~+8% as the lower negotiated prices pass through. Health-contingent wellness designs spread: the tobacco surcharge is waived only with PBM-verified cessation adherence, and BMI-linked premium differentials are kept within HIPAA wellness limits.

pharma.state: Volume up about a third and net price per fill down about 20%. Lilly leads, and Novo has recovered its US supply but faces the EPI signal on its home registries and 2033 US generic entry. MDL reserves were raised. Generic liraglutide makers holding HRSA contracts saw unit prices cut at renewal.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A body now signals a payer and a schedule. The lean, DEXA-tracked build is still concierge retatrutide. A thinner, soft body reads as HRSA liraglutide, a Medicaid kiosk or a cash pen. A body that swells and shrinks on a 90-day rhythm reads as someone on cessation courses. A heavy body worn openly increasingly reads as a declaration.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The finish of the body is still the class marker, but employer retreat moved the middle third from covered weekly pens to $149–249 cash pills, and their results now look like the bottom third's. Charlotte's finance workforce still wears 'the Charlotte build'. Distribution and call-centre workers in Tulsa and Memphis wear the cheaper, softer result.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Small portions are the default. A counter-ritual has grown in Springfield, Missouri, and its suburbs: independent congregations run 'Full Table' Sunday dinners where the stated practice is eating until satisfied without medication. Tens of thousands attend across the Ozarks and Oklahoma. In Oakland and Brooklyn a fat-liberation revival holds 'unmedicated supper clubs' with the opposite politics and the same table.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles list molecule, payer and 'Full Table' or 'off by choice'. 'Cessation cycle' explains a partner's mood swings every 90 days. Mixed couples where one partner is Full Table and the other is on 'focus' are a sitcom premise.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Clinically, appetite is a variable. A visible minority has started treating it as a gift or a right. Pastors preach that 'hunger is how God made you'. Fat-liberation writers call conditioning 'appetite policing'. Anti-pharma 'natural' influencers sell berberine and fasting protocols to the same audience.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Reduced pleasure persists at ~10–15% of long-term users. The 2031 retatrutide SHAPS data showed a small dose-dependent shift. 'Focus/calm/craving-free' subscriptions roughly doubled to ~3.0M adults: ~2.4M in the cash channel at $149–229/month after the price agreement, and ~0.6M via gray-sourced 'microdose' kits. All fit inside the 14.0M cash and 12.8M gray users. The vaping label made 'craving-free' a medical claim for one indication, and the brands lean on that adjacency.
interior_life.framing: A feature with a medical alibi. Ads say 'quit the noise' and borrow the language of the vaping label. Clinicians say 'reward modulation'. Users still call the unwanted version 'the grey'. The Full Table movement calls it 'the dimmer' and treats coming off as testimony.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employers that dropped weight coverage kept or added 'focus' subscription stipends, which cost less and have no claims. Some call centres and logistics firms tie a tobacco-surcharge waiver to verified cessation adherence. Unions in two more national contracts won adherence-data firewalls. Sales and creative workers still schedule dose holidays before pitches.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'off-dose' aesthetic has split. Secular 'unquiet' music and comedy circuits sit alongside a gospel and worship scene in Springfield and Tulsa that bills services as 'unmedicated praise'. Sports-betting handle stays soft in high-uptake states. Vape culture among 18–29s visibly thins at festivals.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists still ask about dose. Couples report fewer fights and less wanting. The 90-day cessation cycle produces a recognisable pattern of calm, then a gap, then irritability. Some couples time anniversaries to the gap.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The movement has no turnout effect but a legislative one. Missouri's Medical Freedom in Benefits Act (2032) bars state-employee plans from using adherence or BMI data, while the state's own Medicaid waiver still does exactly that. Talk radio on both sides attacks conditioning. Candidates are asked whether they are 'on' and, now, whether they are 'Full Table'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on indications (vaping cessation, orforglipron cessation) and defensive on new molecules (MariTide CRL, survodutide and amycretin delays). After the EPI signal it is cautious about long-horizon exposure without restricting it. Price policy works through negotiation, not mandate.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The HRSA programme was renewed at $5.6B for FY2032 with adherence conditions attached. The Medicare Bridge was renewed through 2033 at $215/$50. The ACA preventive mandate now covers semaglutide and orforglipron for smoking and vaping cessation, two 90-day courses a year. There is no mandate to take the drug.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Benefits conditioning is now the norm across programmes. Five Medicaid adherence waivers require ≥80% PDC and quarterly weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout. HRSA requires refill verification for everyone and weigh-ins for liraglutide obesity users, so the two tiers the waiver plaintiffs cited have converged. Employer wellness programmes waive tobacco surcharges on PBM-verified cessation adherence and apply BMI-linked differentials within HIPAA limits. The Indiana disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT apnea clearance still effectively requires tirzepatide for some drivers. The VA added semaglutide for vaping cessation. The Army's recruit policy is unchanged and contested.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The 2031 price agreement traded Section 232 tariff relief for US fill-finish commitments, and Novo's North Carolina site is back in service. Indian generics now dominate most of the world, and Indian mail pens to the US remain a trade-talk item. US generic entry is fixed for 2033.

events.event: FDA extends semaglutide's smoking-cessation indication to e-cigarette and vaping nicotine dependence in adults, covering both the injection and the Wegovy pill; under the ACA preventive mandate, plans must cover it for two 90-day courses a year

CMS and manufacturers sign a second TrumpRx price agreement trading Section 232 tariff relief for US fill-finish capacity: cash semaglutide falls to $249, tirzepatide to $299 and oral starter doses to $149; the Medicare Bridge payment is cut from $275 to $215 when it is renewed in December

CMS approves Missouri, Oklahoma and Tennessee Medicaid 1115 waivers that copy Indiana's ≥80% adherence and quarterly weigh-in rules; three months later Congress renews HRSA's incretin programme at $5.6B with refill-verification and weigh-in conditions attached

Annual benefits surveys show employer weight-management coverage of incretins falling from 57% to 44%, as large self-insured employers limit coverage to diabetes, cardiac and apnea codes and the mandated cessation benefit, often adding 'focus' subscription stipends instead

An estimated 20,000 people attend a 'Full Table' gathering in Springfield, Missouri, against 'medicated appetite' and benefits conditioning; in May the legislature passes a law barring state-employee plans from using adherence or BMI data, while leaving the state's Medicaid waiver in place

A Danish–Swedish registry study finds exocrine pancreatic insufficiency at roughly 1.8 times the expected rate in people on GLP-1 drugs continuously for five years or more; FDA issues a Drug Safety Communication in August and opens a class label review

open_tensions: The EPI signal warns against long continuous use, while the established bone and regain data warn against cycling. Guidance tells ~68M people both to stay on and to be watched for staying on, and plaintiffs are trying to fold chronic pancreatic injury into MDL 3094.

Conditioning has converged across Medicaid, HRSA and employer wellness programmes just as a church-and-fat-liberation backlash wins its first state law. Missouri now bans for its own employees the practice its Medicaid waiver requires, and the Indiana disability challenge is still pending.

Employers retreated from weight coverage partly to wait for 2033 US generic semaglutide. Their workers are bridging on $149–249 cash pills and 18.8% gray product, and nobody owns the gap in muscle, bone or pancreatic monitoring.

'Craving-free' is now a labelled claim for vaping and a marketed mood for ~3M people without obesity. The first SHAPS signal is small and real, the FDA has asked for a study, and 18–29-year-olds are the fastest-growing users.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Retatrutide still lists at $1,499 a month, is supply-allocated, has no TrumpRx cash price, and carries its bone and body-composition monitoring section.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

prose.headline: A Quarter of Adults, Five Years On: The Pill Got Cheaper, the Coverage Got Stricter, and the Pancreas Got a Question
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2032 one American adult in four is on an incretin drug, about sixty-eight million people. Fewer of them are on it because their employer pays for weight loss. The share of employers covering the drugs for weight management fell from fifty-seven percent to forty-four in two years. The plans that dropped it kept paying for diabetes, heart disease and sleep apnea, and they kept paying for quitting because the law requires it. When the FDA extended semaglutide's cessation label to vaping in February 2031, the ACA preventive mandate brought a generation of twenty-something vapers into the drug, two ninety-day courses a year. Use among adults under thirty nearly doubled.

The price came down. It was negotiated down rather than competed down. In March 2031 the administration traded tariff relief for domestic fill-finish commitments, and the cash portal now sells semaglutide at $249, tirzepatide at $299 and starter pills at $149. Medicare cut its Bridge payment to $215. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 and retatrutide is still rationed at $1,499. Generic semaglutide is sold almost everywhere except the United States, where settlements hold it back until 2033. Millions of middle-income workers who lost their employer benefit now pay cash for a daily pill. Nearly thirteen million use compounded pens, Indian mail-order or vials sold for research use.

The state did not stop paying. It started checking. Five states now run Medicaid waivers that require refill records and quarterly weigh-ins, and they lock people out for a year after two misses. Congress renewed the free federal programme at $5.6 billion and attached the same refill verification, which ended the gap between the free clinic and the Medicaid kiosk. Employers that no longer cover weight loss waive the tobacco surcharge only for workers whose pharmacy data show they are taking their quit course. Many of the same employers pay for 'focus' subscriptions, low-dose pills sold to people who were never heavy, as a perk that generates no claims. About three million adults take them.

In May 2032 Danish and Swedish registries reported something nobody had planned a trial around. People on these drugs continuously for five years or more develop exocrine pancreatic insufficiency at nearly twice the expected rate. The rate is still low, the condition is treatable with enzymes, and diabetes itself raises the risk. The FDA issued a safety communication and opened a class review. For years patients were told that stopping brings the weight back and cycling costs bone. Now they are also being told to have their pancreas checked if they stay on. The lawyers in Philadelphia, whose sixty thousand gastroparesis and pancreatitis claims have lost a bellwether, have taken note.

The pushback is local. In Springfield, Missouri, independent congregations hold 'Full Table' Sunday dinners where eating until full without medication is the stated practice, and twenty thousand people came to a rally in March. In Oakland and Brooklyn, fat-liberation supper clubs make the same refusal from the other side of politics. Missouri's legislature passed a law forbidding the state's own employee health plan to look at adherence or BMI data. The state's Medicaid waiver still does both.

Cigarette and vape sales are falling faster than forecast. Spirits and snacks keep contracting, state tobacco-excise budgets are being rewritten, and drugmakers sell more doses for less money each. The country is calmer, thinner and smokes less. Pharmacy data show who is taking their dose, and people can see from your body who pays for it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Kaylee Brandt sets an alarm for 5:10 so she can take the pill with four ounces of water and then wait thirty minutes before coffee. She uses the wait to scroll. Day 71 of 90, the app says, adherence 100%, tobacco surcharge waived. That is seventy-five dollars a paycheck she keeps.

She drives her mother to the Walgreens kiosk on 21st Street before her shift. Her mother steps on the platform, the camera blinks, and the screen says VERIFIED, thank you, Brenda. Her mother says 'Same as last time, practically,' as if she has been accused of something.

At the distribution centre the smokers stand by the dock doors and the vapers stand a little apart from them. There are fewer of both since spring. Devontae offers her his pod out of habit, then remembers. She doesn't want it. She also doesn't want the turkey sandwich, or the song on the radio, or very much of anything. It is not sadness. It is more like the volume is down.

After work she drives out to Broken Arrow because Jess asked her three times. The church fellowship hall has a long table covered in casseroles, rolls and a sheet cake. The pastor says hunger is how God made us and that nobody here is weighing anybody. Kaylee eats half a plate of green beans and feels everyone notice how little she took.

On the drive home she does the maths again. After day 90 comes the gap, and the second course doesn't start until October. She wonders whether she will want the pod back during the gap, and she doesn't know. She is surprised that she hopes she will.
